content.value: Barkpark Tasks Mobile — State of the Epic

One day in: the idea became a research program, the research became a GO, the GO became a founded epic, and the epic's founding wave has already been built and reviewed at A−. The phone app exists as real code on a branch. Right now the wave sits at its merge gate — five PRs open, CI spinning after two ledger-gate blockers were found and cleared — with two risk-retiring spikes queued behind the merges. This paper is the honest snapshot: what exists, what is in flight this minute, and exactly what happens next.

items.label: papers published before a line of code — five investigation lanes plus the crown (GO), all from one deep-investigation run
wave 1 review grade — four slices re-gated green in a fresh worktree with ZERO reviewer fixes
round-1 slices built green: token exchange, Expo skeleton, js unblocks, api unblocks
PRs open right now (#6007–#6011), gate-watcher live and pulsing task leases every 10 minutes
round-2 spikes queued by the sequenced-rounds law: WebView long-paper verdict and the push relay
genuinely new server build in the whole v1 — the member-reachable app-token exchange; it is built and awaiting merge

blocks.source:
flowchart TD
  A["Wish + 4-question interview"] --> B["deep-investigation run: 5 Fable lanes + 25-Sonnet storm"]
  B --> C["5 lane papers + CROWN paper: GO, Operator's Leash on Expo/RN"]
  C --> D["User ratifies: push-in-v1, [read,write,chat] token, 3-tab home"]
  D --> E["bp-epic-cycle wave 1: charter founded, 6 slices cut"]
  E --> F["4 round-1 slices BUILT, reviewed A-, zero fixes"]
  F --> G["*** NOW: 5 PRs at the merge gate (#6007-#6011) ***"]
  G --> H["Merge round 1 == auto-deploy to guerrilla"]
  H --> I["Minted-token smoke + close merge-gated criteria"]
  I --> J["Round 2: WebView spike + push-relay spike"]
  J --> K["Wave 2: paper reader per spike verdict"]

content.value: Epic charter (founded from the crown's rulings)
Wave 1 paper (opened at Strategize, closed as debrief)
Epic parent task + 4 slice tasks + backlog
Published ledger; parent promoted considering→open, claimed by mob-lead
The app itself — Expo SDK 57 skeleton
Built, reviewed, on branch: device-flow login, cascade auto-select + MRU, 3 stub tabs, MMKV/SQLite cache, blocking mobile.yml CI lane
Token exchange (the epic's one hard server build)
Built both halves + 11/11 smoke vs guerrilla; minted-token leg pending deploy
JS + API unblocks (core size gate, heading emitter, D36 chat capability, search fields=, production-first datasets)

All four round-1 slices came back green and the reviewer chased every builder-declared doubt without finding a single fix to make: the JIT-membership race test was proven to fail on the old code with the exact predicted error; the D19a suite drives real minted tokens through every chat route; admin custody is asserted byte-level; the '+chat' manifest suffix was proven unable to reach the wire. The skeleton's UI came in above the bar for a skeleton — honest loading/error/empty/provisioning states with retry affordances everywhere.

Why A− and not A: the wave's second headline risk — the WebView long-paper verdict on real Android hardware — is deliberately still open. It was cut as a round-2 slice behind the heading-emitter fix (charter D12), so the wave closes with its biggest cost fork designed, gated, and queued rather than retired. That is the sequenced-rounds law working as intended, but the grade honestly reflects an unretired risk.
In flight this minute: the merge gate
CI re-running; waits for the Elixir Test gate; merge == auto-deploy of the two new endpoints to guerrilla
CI re-running incl. its own new blocking mobile.yml lane
JS unblocks (core size gate + heading emitter)
CI re-running; Elixir Test already passed 13m green on round 1; unblocks the WebView spike
CI re-running; waits for the Elixir Test gate
CI re-running after the Task:-line fix; merges on its own gate

Two required-gate blockers surfaced after the wave closed, both on the PR↔task ledger gate, both cleared: (1) lease lapse — the builders honestly left their tasks in_progress, but the 2700-second claim leases expired during the wave's tail, the ledger reverted to open, and the gate refused every slice PR; fixed by re-claiming all four tasks as mob-lead and re-firing each branch with an empty commit, since the gate's verdict is sticky and only a push re-fires it. (2) The doc-only charter PR carried no Task: line at all; fixed by referencing the epic parent task — itself claimed — and re-firing. The watcher now pulses all five leases every ten minutes so a lapse cannot recur mid-CI. One spend-limit outage also hit mid-wave, killing the Decide architect and two verifiers; the run resumed from cache with zero loss — 26 completed agents replayed free.
1 · Merge round 1 as gates go green — api/cloud PRs strictly after the Elixir Test gate; merge is the deploy (guerrilla + control plane auto-deploy on main).

2 · Post-merge proofs — rerun the mobile smoke with BP_SMOKE_REQUIRE_EXCHANGE=1 to close the token-exchange criterion with a real minted-token transcript; lead closes every 'PR merged' criterion on the ledger.

3 · Dispatch round 2 — mob-w1-webview-spike the moment the js unblocks land (numeric pass/fail on real mid-tier Android; failure promotes the native prose fast-path into v1 and re-plans wave 2's renderer budget), and mob-w1-push-spike the moment the token exchange lands (schema + one real APNs/FCM sandbox notification off the chat_blocked webhook; both touch the cloud router, hence sequenced).
4 · Wave close-out — boot the skeleton on a MINTED token, retiring the manual-paste fallback so it can never mask exchange bugs.
5 · Wave 2 — the paper reader per the spike verdict, then the chat floor screens: the first wave where the app starts feeling like the crown paper reads.
Risks and human gates on the board
The plan's single biggest cost fork (~2× renderer budget on failure)
Queued round 2, numeric thresholds fixed at Decide
The live plain-member smoke needs a second real Cloud member seat on guerrilla — only a human can add one
No HTTP revoke exists; it is the pre-ship kill switch
The one place v1 exceeds 'just a client'; severable by design (registration-row-absent = off)
Spike queued round 2; build is wave 2
Killed one wave mid-Decide today; recurs
Playbook proven: probe, then resume from cache

The honest one-paragraph state: the thinking is done and published, the decisions are ratified, the one hard server build is written, and the phone app is real code with real CI — nothing is imagined anymore. The epic's entire near-term motion is mechanical: gates green → merge → smoke → two spikes → wave 2. The only human hands needed are the member seat, the ratifications already given, and — when the WebView numbers land — one look at the verdict.
